canDo: Can talk about near plans, longer-term goals and simple predictions.
review: Review the present; contrast the futur proche with the futur simple.
input: Listening: changes of plan; reading: event plans/project descriptions.
output: Write 100 words about future plans; talk for 2 minutes about next week and next year.
checkpoint: Use at least two ways of expressing the future; be able to say why you chose them.
challenge: Today’s challenge: write down in French 3 concrete plans for next week (futur proche) and 2 goals for next year (futur simple), add a prediction (Je pense que…), then talk about it into your phone for 1 minute; when you’ve finished, pin the list up by your desk.

questions.why: « les concerts commenceront plus tôt … pour que les familles puissent rester ». The street performances keep the same times; côté jardin is where the food area is.
« afin que l'on puisse discuter sans crier » states the purpose clearly.
Only Thursday is free; the other three evenings need tickets bought online from 2 May. The producers run the food, not the ticket sales.
Just over six weeks is the work on the whole building; fifteen days is the notice period; each flat needs only one day.
The only solution the text gives is to leave the keys with someone you trust and tell the caretaker. The curtains must be taken down the day before.
The letter only mentions lower heating bills, because the new windows insulate better. Neither the rent nor the light is mentioned.
At present it’s a fifteen-minute walk or a change to line 14. A bus every twelve minutes is after the extension; the Fontaine stop hasn’t been built yet.
« La fréquence actuelle, elle, ne changera pas sur le reste du parcours ». The last bus will be forty minutes later, and there will be three more stops.
After the extension it will be 23 h 10, forty minutes later than now, so it is currently 22 h 30. This question needs a subtraction.
The opening is explicit: « Ne commencez pas par choisir une école : commencez par le métier visé. » Funding is the third step, meetings the second.
The text says many people discover at exactly this step that the job differs from what they imagined. Finding an employer and shortening the course aren’t mentioned.
One hour is the length of an interview, two or three the number of meetings. The overall preparation takes three to six months.
Two volunteers have dropped out, leaving only six. The stall layout will be sent that evening; it isn’t the problem.
She says she’ll bring her brother and arrive herself at 6 h 30 — « je ne peux pas plus tôt ». 8 is the expected finishing time.
« Si ton frère vient, on tiendra les horaires » — the condition is one more person.
From the second week the street is closed to all vehicles; pedestrians can still use the right-hand pavement. One-way traffic is the arrangement for the first week.
« La collecte ne changera pas de jour, mais les bacs devront être sortis au coin de la rue » — it’s the place that changes.
The announcement gives Thursday of the second week at 18 h 30.
Every year they turn away about a hundred people for lack of slots at the venue. The fee isn’t changing, and he’s confident about the building.
« C'est le point le plus délicat : les profils que nous cherchons sont rares. » He is confident about the building.
The journalist says confiant; he corrects it to « Prudent, plutôt ». Funding isn’t mentioned.
Her father works until 20 on Thursday. Her brother’s classes finish at 17 on Friday.
« plus tu attendras, plus ce sera cher ». Monday is when the whole family comes back.
She only asks whether he eats fish, to plan the Saturday meal.
